notes: Also commonly used as an adverb meaning 'alone' ('yalnız yaşamak' — to live alone), meaning 'only' ('yalnız sen' — only you), or as a conjunction meaning 'but / however'.

senses.definition: Without other people; on one's own.

examples.translation: I was alone at home all day.
examples.emotion: somewhat dejected and quiet, looking out a rainy window

senses.definition: Unhappy because one has no friends or company.

examples.text: Yeni taşındığı şehirde kendini çok yalnız hissediyor.
examples.translation: She feels very lonely in the city she just moved to.

draftBefore.emotion: quiet and melancholy, feeling the silence of an empty room
notes: Yalnız can mean both physically alone and emotionally lonely depending on the context.
Do not confuse it with sadece, which strictly means 'only' when used as an adverb.

faults.why: 'Yalnız' does not mean 'sole/only' as an attributive adjective before a noun ('tek' is used); it means 'only' as an adverb/particle.

faults.quote: Evde bütün gün yalnız kaldım. — I stayed lonely at home all day.
faults.why: 'Yalnız kalmak' means 'to be left alone / stay by oneself', not 'stayed lonely' ('yalnız hissetmek' shows 'lonely').
In 'yalnız yürümek', 'yalnız' functions as an adverb modifying the verb, whereas the entry POS is adjective.
